candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — cardiac biomarkers
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize serial cardiac troponin, preferably high-sensitivity troponin, as the preferred biomarker strategy for acute myocardial injury assessment.

options.A: A single CK-MB value is preferred over troponin because it is the most cardiac-specific biomarker available.
options.B: Myoglobin alone can definitively diagnose acute myocardial infarction without serial testing or clinical correlation.
options.C: Serial cardiac troponin I or T testing is preferred for myocardial injury, and high-sensitivity troponin is preferred when available.
options.D: Total creatine kinase is more specific for myocardial injury than cardiac troponin and should replace troponin testing.

candidate.rationale: The AHA/ACC chest-pain guideline recommends serial cardiac troponin I or T for myocardial injury and prefers high-sensitivity troponin because of its diagnostic performance and faster detection. CK-MB, myoglobin, and total CK are not preferred replacements for contemporary cardiac troponin testing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Serial cTn I/T is the preferred myocardial-injury biomarker approach and high-sensitivity troponin is preferred.
candidate.source_document_title: 2021 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain
candidate.source_locator: Biomarkers / key recommendation: serial cardiac troponin I or T preferred; high-sensitivity troponin preferred
candidate.source_organization: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association (ACC/AHA)
